clue.text: Everyone in drag is fat

indicators.note: the word for everyone sits inside the word for drag

parts.note: to drag something is to tow it
everyone means all

explanation.surface: A remark that everyone dressed in drag is overweight.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallow is rendered animal fat, used for candles and soap.

clue.text: Cotton on back of weather glass

parts.note: to tumble to something is British slang for to cotton on, to understand

indicators.note: back of means the final letter of weather

explanation.surface: Something fixed on the back of a barometer, the weather glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weather glass' looks like one phrase, a barometer; 'glass' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbler is a flat-bottomed drinking vessel, one kind of glass.

clue.text: Free love recurring in college

indicators.note: in puts the repeated letter inside the college abbreviation

parts.note: LSE is the London School of Economics, a college of London University

indicators.note: recurring means the love letter appears again, so twice

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Free love keeps cropping up at college.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose means unconfined, at liberty, synonymous with free.

clue.text: One taken in by Orlando anagram? Not last but possibly first

indicators.note: taken in by puts the letter for one inside the jumbled name
anagram tells us the name's letters are rearranged
not last means the name loses its final letter

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: The setter, Orlando, plays with an anagram of his own name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not last' drops the final O of ORLANDO; I goes inside an arrangement of ORLAND.
explanation.definitionFit: First is an example of a number word giving position in a series.

clue.text: Crash after stock's first issued

indicators.note: after places the crash word following the single letter
first means only the opening letter of stock is taken

parts.note: prang is British slang for a crash, especially of a car or plane

explanation.surface: A market crash coming after the stock was first put on sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprang means came forth or arose, as water issued from a source.

clue.text: Jeremy's 100 for 10 in video game

indicators.note: 100 for 10 means the numeral for a hundred takes the place of the numeral for ten

parts.note: Jeremy Paxman is a British television interviewer and quizmaster
X is the Roman numeral ten
C is the Roman numeral a hundred

explanation.surface: Swapping numbers within a video game.
explanation.definitionFit: The maze-chasing arcade title from 1980 is a classic electronic game.

clue.text: Metal I dropped over the Atlantic

definitions.text: Metal I dropped over the Atlantic

parts.words: Metal I dropped over the Atlantic
parts.note: Americans spell this metal without its second I, so across the ocean that letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A piece of metal falls from a plane over the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: The American spelling of the metal omits one I, so 'I dropped over the Atlantic' describes the spelling, not a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: This light silvery element, spelt with -ium in Britain, is a metal.

clue.text: Leader of Girl Guides in Wells

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of girl

parts.note: ushers guide people to seats

explanation.surface: The head of the Girl Guides troop in Wells, the cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl Guides' looks like one name, and Wells like a place; Wells is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gushers are oil wells that spout freely, so they are examples of wells.

clue.text: Waters I can omit?

parts.note: read the second word of the answer as an anagram signal: the first word, made fluid, gives the letters of I can omit

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they may leave out some waters.
explanation.definitionFit: When a woman's waters break, it is the liquid round the unborn baby being released.

clue.text: Magazine articles from William Morris

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the run of the name William Morris

explanation.surface: Pieces written for a magazine by the Victorian designer William Morris.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun's magazine holds cartridges, so its contents are ammunition, shortened colloquially.

clue.text: A crude mop's deployed — that stops water rising

indicators.note: deployed means the letters of a crude mop's are spread out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wields a rough mop to deal with water coming up.
explanation.definitionFit: A damp-proof layer in a wall's base, it blocks moisture from climbing up through brickwork.

clue.text: Brief encounter, at first, with one in Shropshire location

indicators.note: in puts the two letters inside the name of the Shropshire town

parts.note: Clun is a small town in Shropshire, an English county bordering Wales

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of encounter is used

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Evokes the film Brief Encounter, with someone at a Shropshire spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like part of the film title but is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To brief someone is to give them the information they need, the idiom for informing them.

clue.text: Unreal Christmas visitors ate outside, refusing starter

indicators.note: outside says the eating word wraps round the visitors
refusing starter means the eating word loses its first letter

parts.note: dined means ate
the Magi, the three wise men, visited the infant Jesus in the Christmas story

explanation.surface: Fanciful Christmas guests who ate outdoors but skipped the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christmas visitors' are the three wise men of the Nativity story; 'refusing starter' drops the first letter of the eating word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imagined exists only in the mind, so it is not real.

clue.text: Convert writing? Only text without margins

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language

indicators.note: without margins means the outer edges of the phrase only text are cut away, two letters from each end

explanation.surface: A query whether converting writing means just the text, with no margins.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip ON and XT from the edges of 'Only text' to leave LYTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A proselyte is a person converted to a new religion or belief, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Junior minister abused working party

indicators.note: working means the letters of abused are worked into a new order

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, a political party

explanation.surface: A junior government minister mistreated a group at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Junior minister' suggests government; here it is the church rank below deacon.
explanation.definitionFit: A subdeacon is a cleric ranking under a deacon, a lower ministry.

clue.text: Skittles as stocking-fillers?

definitions.meaning: the wooden targets knocked down in skittles or bowling
legs, in slang, fill stockings; the question mark flags the playful sense

explanation.definitionFit: Pins are both the targets in skittles and a slang word for legs, which fill stockings.

clue.text: School expelling good girl

indicators.note: expelling throws the letter for good out of the school name

parts.note: Rugby is a famous English public school in Warwickshire

explanation.surface: A school expels a well-behaved girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruby is a girl's given name.

clue.text: Dance away, say, without apparent effort

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
off means away, as in going off

explanation.surface: Dancing off effortlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite a list fluently and quickly is to speak it with ease.

clue.text: Hayek, say, giving English company clear conditions

parts.note: clear weather conditions are ones with no mist

explanation.surface: Hayek offering an English firm a clean bill of conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Hayek was an Austrian-British theorist of markets, an example of the profession.

clue.text: Seminarian and judge provide commentary?

parts.note: read as semi-narian, half of narian, which is its first three letters
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: A trainee priest and a judge commentate together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seminarian' is split as 'semi' plus 'narian': half of NARIAN is NAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to give a spoken account, as a commentator does.

clue.text: Unpleasant short story accepted by team

indicators.note: accepted by puts the shortened story inside the team word

parts.note: a squad is a team

indicators.note: short means the story word loses its last letter

parts.note: a story can mean a lie

explanation.surface: A grubby little tale taken on by a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts the last letter from the story word, a lie being a made-up story.
explanation.definitionFit: Squalid means sordid and filthy, so thoroughly disagreeable.

clue.text: Not quite missing line of stars

indicators.note: not quite means the word for missing loses its final letter

parts.note: astray means missing or lost

explanation.surface: A line of stars is almost gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line of stars' looks like a phrase; 'of stars' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Astral is the adjective relating to the heavenly bodies.

clue.text: Backing last couple of singers in show

indicators.note: in puts the final pair of letters inside the word for show

parts.note: to reveal is to show

indicators.note: last couple of means the final two letters of singers

explanation.surface: Backing singers, the last pair of them, appearing in a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like part of 'backing singers' but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A reversal is a going backwards, the same sense as backing as a noun.

clue.text: Row made by curious cat with no tail

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or curious

indicators.note: with no tail means the cat word loses its last letter

parts.note: puss is a familiar word for a cat

explanation.surface: A fight caused by a strange tailless cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpus is a noisy commotion, the same as a row in the sense of a quarrel.

clue.text: Most important character in Fawlty Towers

definitions.meaning: chief or principal, greatest in importance
the doddering retired army officer living at the hotel in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers

explanation.definitionFit: Major means principal, and the Major is a resident in the 1970s British sitcom Fawlty Towers.

clue.text: Unison in a collapse

parts.note: to act in concert is to act in unison

explanation.surface: Everyone falling down together at once.
explanation.definitionFit: To concertina is to fold up or crumple in pleats, like the squeezebox, a verb for collapse.

clue.text: 1 down with Jack, in a bad way

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in playing cards
ill means unwell, in a bad way

explanation.surface: Recalls the nursery rhyme where Jack fell and Jill came tumbling after.
explanation.walkthrough: In the rhyme, Jack fell down and Jill came tumbling after, so she is the one who tumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Jill came tumbling after in the rhyme, so she is the tumbling one of the pair.

clue.text: Going west, panache provided conclusion

indicators.note: going west in an across answer means reading from right to left

parts.note: elan is dash or panache
if means provided that

explanation.surface: Heading west with style made for a fine ending.
explanation.definitionFit: A finale is the last part of a show or piece of music, its end.

clue.text: Scorched watercolour?

parts.note: split into water, the sea, and colour, red; the Red Sea read as a coloured body of water
the colour part gives red

explanation.surface: A painting looks burnt.
explanation.definitionFit: Seared means burned on the surface by intense heat.
